Your privacy matters. This page explains how Keyboard X handles information when you use the app and keyboard.

Keyboard settings and preferences may be stored locally on your device to make the app work. The app should only describe information collection or sharing that is actually implemented in its current version.

A keyboard can process the text you type to provide input functionality. Never enter passwords or sensitive information unless you trust the app and understand its behavior. This policy must be updated if the app adds analytics, network services, cloud processing, or other data collection.
You can disable Keyboard X in Android keyboard settings and remove locally stored app data through Android settings. Available in-app data controls will be listed here when implemented.

Find help with setup, keyboard activation, language switching, and appearance settings.
How do I enable Keyboard X?
Open Android Settings, go to the keyboard management screen, and enable Keyboard X. Then use the system keyboard picker to select it.
Choose Arabic or English in the Languages section. Language switching while typing depends on the language key supported by the active keyboard layout.
Does the keyboard send what I type to a server?
Check the published privacy policy for the exact behavior of the installed version. The policy must be kept aligned with the actual code and any network features.
